sols.title: Sol 1: The Night Freeze
sols.subtitle: Martian Night Surface Temp: -60°C
sols.briefing: Cmdr. Reyes: 'First shift at Jezero Crater! It is freezing outside at -60°C. Keep our sweet potatoes alive in CAM 03, but huwag ubusin ang battery sa heaters bago mag-sunrise!'

victory.title: 🌅 6:00 AM — SOL 1 SURVIVED!
victory.description: Galing! You balanced battery reserves and pulsed the greenhouse heaters so the crops survived the sub-zero Martian night.
victory.nasaCitation: NASA Benchmark: Temperatures at the Martian equator drop from 20°C at noon down to -73°C at night. Without active heating, greenhouse crops die within hours.

failureBattery.title: ⚡ TOTAL HABITAT BLACKOUT
failureBattery.description: You left the heavy heaters running constantly! The outpost battery died in the dark before sunrise.
failureBattery.nasaCitation: NASA Fact: Mars solar arrays produce 0 Watts at night. Outposts must carefully budget stored battery power until dawn.

failureFreeze.title: 🥶 GREENHOUSE FROZE SOLID (-10°C)!
failureFreeze.description: You neglected CAM 03! The sweet potato tubers and chlorella cultures froze solid in the cold.
failureFreeze.nasaCitation: NASA Benchmark: NASA plant growth chambers (like Veggie on the ISS) require tight thermal regulation between 18°C and 24°C to prevent root frostbite.

failureO2.title: 🫁 HYPOXIA ALERT
failureO2.nasaCitation: NASA Fact: Mars atmosphere is 95% CO2. Humans require closed-loop oxygen systems.

failureRadiation.title: ☢️ RADIATION BREACH
failureRadiation.nasaCitation: NASA Fact: Mars lacks a global magnetosphere to shield against cosmic rays.

sols.title: Sol 2: The Red Dust Front
sols.subtitle: Atmospheric Dust Opacity (Tau) Rising
sols.briefing: Engr. Cruz: 'A local dust swirl is sweeping over Sector Jezero! Dust is sticking to our exterior regulators on CAM 01. When it hits, deploy the Wiper Drone agad to stop extra power drain!'

victory.title: 🌅 6:00 AM — SOL 2 SURVIVED!
victory.description: Impressive! You kept the crops warm while wiping red dust off the power couplings before it drained the outpost dry.
victory.nasaCitation: NASA Benchmark: Dust accumulation on Mars severely degraded the Opportunity and InSight missions, reducing solar output by up to 99%. Automated wipers or electrostatic dust cleaners are essential for long missions.

failureBattery.title: ⚡ POWER EXHAUSTION (0% BATTERY)
failureBattery.description: Dust coated the power couplings and drained your battery before you could wipe them clean!
failureBattery.nasaCitation: NASA Fact: Dust-covered panels and clogged thermal radiators dramatically increase electrical parasitic draw.

failureFreeze.title: 🥶 GREENHOUSE FROZE SOLID
failureFreeze.description: While checking CAM 01, you forgot to pulse the greenhouse heaters on CAM 03!
failureFreeze.nasaCitation: NASA Benchmark: Mars' thin atmosphere holds virtually no heat, causing temperatures to plummet the moment heating stops.

failureO2.title: 🫁 HYPOXIA ALERT
failureO2.nasaCitation: NASA Fact: Closed-loop ECLSS systems must maintain continuous air flow.

failureRadiation.title: ☢️ RADIATION BREACH
failureRadiation.nasaCitation: NASA Fact: Radiation exposure accumulates over mission duration.

sols.title: Sol 3: Filter Infiltration
sols.subtitle: CO₂ Recycler Differential Pressure Spike
sols.briefing: Botanist Santos: 'Fine Martian regolith got sucked into the life support intake on CAM 02! The O2 filter is clogging up fast. Use the manual thump or toggle Turbo Scrubber bago tayo maubusan ng hangin!'

victory.title: 🌅 6:00 AM — SOL 3 SURVIVED!
victory.description: Mahusay! You kept the air breathable, brushed off the dust, and kept the greenhouse warm all at once.
victory.nasaCitation: NASA Benchmark: The Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment (MOXIE) on Perseverance produced oxygen directly from atmospheric CO2. On human missions, ECLSS recyclers must constantly scrub CO2 and maintain a 21% O2 / 78% N2 cabin mix.

failureO2.title: 🫁 HYPOXIA — OXYGEN DEPLETED (0%)!
failureO2.description: The air intake clogged with fine Martian regolith and you did not clear it or run the Turbo Scrubber in time!
failureO2.nasaCitation: NASA Fact: Mars air is 95% toxic carbon dioxide. Without active oxygen recycling, astronauts experience cognitive decline in minutes.

failureBattery.title: ⚡ BATTERY DEPLETED
failureBattery.description: Running the Turbo Scrubber non-stop while keeping heaters on drained the outpost battery.
failureBattery.nasaCitation: NASA Benchmark: Running high-draw life support systems continuously requires tight power prioritization.

failureFreeze.title: 🥶 CROPS FROZEN
failureFreeze.description: You focused too much on oxygen and let the greenhouse freeze.
failureFreeze.nasaCitation: NASA Fact: Multitasking thermal and atmospheric controls is the primary role of space habitat flight controllers.

failureRadiation.title: ☢️ RADIATION BREACH
failureRadiation.nasaCitation: NASA Fact: Cosmic radiation requires steady baseline habitat shielding.

sols.title: Sol 4: The Solar Particle Wave
sols.subtitle: Coronal Mass Ejection (CME) Impact
sols.briefing: Cmdr. Reyes: 'NASA Space Weather Alert: A solar flare just erupted! Radiation outside is spiking on CAM 04. Slam the Lead Blast Shutter CLOSED when it strikes, pero OPEN it agad when it clears kasi +2 bars ang drain niyan!'

victory.title: 🌅 6:00 AM — SOL 4 SURVIVED!
victory.description: Tactical perfection! You slammed the blast shutter shut to block the solar flare, and reopened it right in time to conserve battery for sunrise.
victory.nasaCitation: NASA Benchmark: Unlike Earth, Mars lacks a protective global magnetic field. During solar particle events, radiation doses can exceed 100 mSv. Astronauts must take shelter in regolith bunkers or heavy shielded storm shelters.

failureRadiation.title: ☢️ CRITICAL RADIATION BREACH (0%)!
failureRadiation.description: A high-energy solar particle wave struck Outpost Bulalakaw while the Lead Blast Shutter was left OPEN!
failureRadiation.nasaCitation: NASA Fact: Solar energetic particles travel near the speed of light. Without physical shielding, radiation breaches cause immediate electronics damage and acute crew radiation sickness.

failureBattery.title: ⚡ POWER COLLAPSE (+2 USAGE PENALTY)
failureBattery.description: You forgot to OPEN the Lead Blast Shutter after the solar flare passed! The heavy motorized locks drained your battery completely.
failureBattery.nasaCitation: NASA Benchmark: Heavy mechanical systems like blast doors and airlocks consume substantial electrical reserves and must be powered down when not actively needed.

failureFreeze.title: 🥶 CROPS FROZEN
failureFreeze.description: You panicked during the solar storm and neglected greenhouse temperatures.
failureFreeze.nasaCitation: NASA Fact: Outpost commanders must stay calm and balance multiple simultaneous room hazards.

failureO2.title: 🫁 OXYGEN DEPLETED
failureO2.description: The air loop clogged while you were handling the blast shutter.
failureO2.nasaCitation: NASA Fact: ECLSS atmospheric monitoring cannot be ignored even during external radiation storms.

sols.title: Sol 5: The Martian Gauntlet
sols.subtitle: Maximum Environmental Stress Shift
sols.briefing: All Station Comms: 'This is it, Commander! All hazards are active tonight: freezing temperatures, dust storms, clogged filters, and radiation flares! Manage all 4 rooms and bring Outpost Bulalakaw safely to sunrise!'

victory.title: 🏆 OUTPOST BULALAKAW COMMANDER CERTIFICATION!
victory.description: Mabuhay, Commander! You survived all 5 Sols on Mars, mastering Power, Life Support, Food, and Radiation Shielding under extreme pressure. Mission successful!
victory.nasaCitation: NASA Systems Engineering Takeaway: Mission success on Mars is not about infinite resources—it is about managing trade-offs. You proved that balancing battery storage, thermal control, closed-loop air recycling, and radiation protection keeps astronauts alive!

failureBattery.title: ⚡ HABITAT BLACKOUT ON SOL 5
failureBattery.description: The gauntlet pushed your electrical grid past its breaking point.
failureBattery.nasaCitation: NASA Benchmark: Complex human missions require active power shedding protocols when multiple subsystems demand peak draw simultaneously.

failureFreeze.title: 🥶 CROPS FROZEN ON SOL 5
failureFreeze.description: The greenhouse temperature dropped below -10°C during the final hour.
failureFreeze.nasaCitation: NASA Fact: Automated thermal loops are essential to keep biological systems alive while crew members handle mechanical crises.

failureO2.title: 🫁 HYPOXIA ON SOL 5
failureO2.description: Oxygen levels bottomed out in the final stretch.
failureO2.nasaCitation: NASA Fact: Human spaceflight requires rapid fault detection and isolation in life support loops.

failureRadiation.title: ☢️ RADIATION BREACH ON SOL 5
failureRadiation.description: The final coronal mass ejection overwhelmed unshielded crew quarters.
failureRadiation.nasaCitation: NASA Fact: Redundant radiation shelters and active warning sensors are paramount for deep space surface missions.
